post.caption: This jewel says who ordered it made. The Alfred Jewel has an Old English inscription around its edge that reads, Alfred ordered me to be made. Gold frames a tiny enamel figure under a cover of rock crystal, and the green-robed figure may stand for the sense of sight. It was reportedly plowed up in a field in Somerset in 1693. Its base is a dragon-like head with a socket for a rod, so it may have topped an aestel, a pointer for following the words in a book. In the preface to his Pastoral Care, Alfred wrote that each copy would carry an aestel worth fifty mancuses, and a mancus was worth roughly a month's wages. Today the jewel is on display in the Ashmolean Museum in Oxford.
